subject: Urgent: Hosted API ramp delay causing p95/p99 regressions — Financio
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@financio.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@financio.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spikes this morning — urgent

Hi Sean,

We started seeing severe degradation on our production workload around 08:20 PT this morning. P95 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.1s and p99 to ~6.8s for text-generation calls; throughput dropped by ~30% as retries piled up. The errors are 502/504 during scale-up windows. This is impacting our end-users and we need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA for a stable resolution.

I've attached a sampling of request traces and a dashboard snapshot. We haven't changed any traffic shape or prompts on our side. Please escalate if needed — our CS is on standby.

Samantha
Director of Platform Engineering
Financio

Samantha — thanks for the data and flag. We're treating this as a high-priority escalation. Initial read: the traces point to a prolonged cold-start/initialization delay during autoscale events on the GPU pool serving your model variant. I'm looping in SRE and Infra.

- Dylan will pull live traces and confirm whether fallback routing is occurring.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spikes this morning — urgent

Quick sync notes from the infra side:

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler started provisioning new GPU instances at ~08:18 PT for Financio's pool. New instances reported successful boot, but the runtime's model warmup step (kv-cache hydration + custom kernel selection) had a 90th percentile stall of ~4.5s and a heavy tail out to ~24s on some hosts.
- During this window we saw requests routed to newly spun instances without an enforced warm-pool or preflight check; that caused client-facing p95/p99 to spike and upstream LB to return 502 when the node was still in warmup.
- Recent change 'runtime:selective-kernel-update' (deployed 08-23) alters kernel probe order — suspected contributor.

Immediate mitigations deployed at 09:40 PT:
1) Temporarily disabled routing to cold instances for Financio-specific pool and enabled fallback to a smaller, already-warmed capacity tier.
2) Increased warm-pool min instances for the account from 1->3 for the next 2 hours.
3) Pushed a short-lived config to skip kernel re-probing on first attach (hotfix flag).

I'll attach a short trace export and a link to the runtime logs. Requesting Laura to check whether the node image staging caused longer-than-expected kernel compilation times.

Dylan
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachment: runtime_warmup_excerpt_0824.txt
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spikes this morning — urgent

Investigated the node staging timeline and kernel cache:
- Node boot and container startup times are within baseline. The hotspot is kernel link-time for the new microkernel set — some kernel variants hit a cold compile path when the model sequence-length distribution was unexpectedly long.
- There was a bump in compilation queue length between 08:10-08:40 due to a coincident maintenance window on a compilation shard. That aligns with Financio's incident window.

Proposed medium-term fixes:
- Revert selective-kernel-update until we can validate on a non-customer shard.
- Populate compile cache proactively for Financio's model variants (pre-warm compile images).
- Add a pre-check on routing that enforces model-ready health probe before sending production traffic.

I'll prepare a short MOP (method of procedure) for the kernel revert and pre-warm steps; can we schedule a canary at 03:00 PT tomorrow to avoid user impact?

Laura
Engineering Manager, Runtime

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@financio.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@financio.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spikes this morning — urgent

Samantha / Tom — follow-up and actions after the incident review: 

What we did (summary):
- Identified that a runtime kernel-probing change + an unrelated compilation shard maintenance produced a cold-start tail during autoscale, leading to p95/p99 regressions.
- Short-term mitigations on Aug 24: disabled routing to cold nodes, increased warm-pool minimum for Financio, and applied a hotfix flag to avoid first-attach kernel probing.
- Long-term changes we will enact: revert the selective-kernel-update, populate compile-cache proactively for your model variants, add routing pre-checks and an account-aware warm-pool policy.

Timeline & commitments: 
- Revert and scoped canary: 2026-08-26 03:00 PT (final plan + MOP shared by Laura by 22:00 PT tonight).
- Compile cache pre-population: delivery ETA 2026-09-02; will be scoped and prioritized on your SLA tier.
- Follow-up postmortem and telemetry export: 2026-08-27 EOD.

Compensation: Evelyn will propose a short-term usage credit to compensate for customer impact — we'll share the proposal in the next update.

If you want an exec-level sync tomorrow morning, cc me and Evelyn and we'll schedule. Again — apologies for the disruption. We're taking steps to avoid recurrence.

Best,
Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf (MOP + timeline)
